page: Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 hardware running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical x86_64 cores clocked at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-physical-core topology. Its cache subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 vector support, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and AES cryptography, offering targeted hardware acceleration for vector math and data security without utilizing simultaneous multithreading.

Memory allocation is fixed at 16.0 GB total, delivering 4.0 GB per core. In synthetic memory testing, small cached blocks reached 853.2 GB/sec, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes achieved 53.01 GB/sec and 34.32 GB/sec respectively. Bundled with the instance is 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed ephemeral capacity suitable for swap, runtime scratchpads, and rapid temporary data indexing without incurring external block storage latencies.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core performance, where stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests placed the instance in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Single-threaded compression workloads also excelled, reaching 40.89 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.86 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core metrics—such as multi-threaded bzip3, PassMark CPU scores, and Clang software compilation—remained in the middle 50% tier due to the 4-core boundary. Lightweight machine learning inference with small models performed well in token generation, though medium-scale 7B model prompt processing fell into the lower 25%.

The architectural profile yields high resource efficiency for workloads constrained by raw single-thread clock frequency rather than sheer parallel density. The lack of a dedicated GPU and the moderate 16 GB memory ceiling limit applicability for large model training or memory-bound analytical databases. However, the combination of dedicated high-frequency cores and high-speed local NVMe storage makes Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 an effective fit for static web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch compression, and microservices requiring predictable compute latencies.
description: Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 16 GB of system memory alongside a direct-attached 472 GB NVMe SSD. The x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, reflecting in top-tier benchmark results for single-core execution, text processing, and single-threaded data compression. Multi-core compute throughput and memory bandwidth align with mid-range baselines, while the local NVMe storage provides low-latency workspace for temporary files and disk-intensive caching. The lack of a discrete GPU and modest core count limits large-scale parallel processing or heavy artificial intelligence training, but the machine achieves high efficiency in compute-focused workloads. Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is well suited for web serving, continuous integration build jobs, software compilation, database caching layers, and high-frequency compute tasks.
